settings.heading: Three ways to read a pan
settings.text:
One pan, three views. Human shows the finish. Engineer shows the construction. Machine opens the structured record. Design targets carry their status across the catalogue.

Explore the catalogue · See the agent-facing demo

settings.heading: Change the hob. Watch the heat spread.
settings.text:
Give both modelled bases the same burner. Change the heat pattern and watch what happens to the cold spots. Use the piece’s own specifications to check hob fit.

Try the heat demo · Find a piece for your hob

settings.heading: Chulha starts with what’s cooking
settings.text:
Turn the paratha. Pour the chai. Layer the rice. Chulha starts with those gestures and asks what clay can do for each one.

Testing is still open. We want potters to help shape the designs, agree the terms and receive credit wherever the pieces are shown.

settings.heading: Measure the pan twice
settings.text:
The rim tells you how much room there is for the dosa. The base and the handle tell you how much room the pan needs on the hob.

Forge starts with clad steel. Laser etching is a design study. Layer counts, dimensions and heat ratings carry their evidence status in the record.

See the Forge catalogue

settings.heading: A way back from the pan
settings.text: Kansa draws on prepared guidance. We’re exploring a code to take the next owner from the pan to its record. A proposed 3D view could show how far the handle reaches across a hob.

settings.heading: Help people choose before they commit
settings.text:
One tawa at home. A row of matching pans for service. The Foundry gives shoppers the available sizes, a running subtotal and room for a gift note. Trade enquiries start with pieces, quantities and a date.

Open the set builder · Make a trade enquiry

settings.heading: Make participation worthwhile on both sides
settings.text: A shop has to work for the person buying and the person making. We’d test who pays for discovery and support, and what changes when makers sell elsewhere. That pricing question comes from Rochet and Tirole (2003).

settings.heading: Who keeps hold of the record?
settings.text: Our aim is to credit the maker, give them a record they can take elsewhere and let the cook read care instructions without a sign-in. The question of who keeps the record comes from Nick Srnicek (2017).

settings.heading: One catalogue for the shop, the cook and the agent
settings.text:
The brief scoped an $85,000 concept engagement for retail and trade, with a target order value of $150–$2,200. One catalogue serves the storefront, care prototype and agent demo.

HexClad and Made In were references for material and merchandising. Healf, Our Place, Caraway and Material Kitchen informed the page and photographs. Great Jones and Smithey offered references for recipes, finish and care.

The test is simple. Can a cook tell if the pan fits? Can the next cook find the care instructions?

settings.heading: Building Maison Tavo
settings.lede: One question about a hob became a shop, a material study and a record that can follow the pan home.
